title: Concatenation of Consecutive Binary Numbers
summary: Provide the decimal equivalent of the binary string created by joining the binary forms of numbers from 1 to n, with the result capped at 10^9 + 7.
statement: Provide the decimal equivalent of the binary string created by joining the binary forms of numbers from 1 to n, with the result capped at 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Concatenate the ordinary binary forms of 1 through n and return the resulting integer modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: Appending value’s binary digits shifts the current result left by that value’s bit length.
Track bit length, increasing it exactly at powers of two.
For value 1..n, update bits on powers of two and set answer=((answer<<bits)|value) mod M.
The shift opens exactly the required digit positions and OR copies value into them, matching string concatenation.
editorial: The shift opens exactly the required digit positions and OR copies value into them, matching string concatenation.

tests.explanation: The concatenation is binary 1, whose value is one.
Binary forms 1,10,11 concatenate to 11011, decimal twenty-seven.
